rubric.why: This distinguishes the biological field by its use of mathematics.
rubric.description: Defines Biomathematics as applying mathematics to biology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the use of mathematical methods or models to solve biological problems.

rubric.why: This distinguishes Bioeconomics by its use of economic principles in biology.
rubric.description: Defines Bioeconomics as applying economics to biological resources or problems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the economic study or management of biological resources.

modelAnswer: Biomathematics applies mathematical methods and models to solve problems in biology.
Bioeconomics applies economic principles to the study and management of biological resources.

items.followUp: State two ways horticulture benefits people.

rubric.description: Identifies the provision of fruits and vegetables as a benefit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that horticulture provides food, particularly fruits and vegetables.

rubric.why: Horticulture also has economic and aesthetic benefits.
rubric.description: Identifies an additional benefit such as income, employment or beautification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid economic or aesthetic benefit.

modelAnswer: Horticulture provides people with fruits and vegetables for food.
It also provides income and employment, and ornamental plants beautify the surroundings.

items.followUp: Name the two types of selection used to explain Darwin's theory of evolution.

rubric.why: Natural selection is a central mechanism in Darwin's theory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying natural selection.

rubric.why: Darwin also used artificial selection as a comparison for selection in nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying artificial selection.

modelAnswer: Darwin used natural selection as a tool to explain evolution.
He also used artificial selection, in which humans select organisms with desired traits.

items.followUp: List four features of a scientific hypothesis.

rubric.why: A good hypothesis has several qualities that make it useful for scientific investigation.
rubric.description: Gives four valid characteristics of a good hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 0.5 mark for each distinct valid characteristic, up to 2 marks. Examples include clear, simple, testable, falsifiable, based on observations, and predictive.

modelAnswer: A good hypothesis is clear and simple.
It is testable and can be falsified.

items.followUp: What cell structures were discovered by Camillo Golgi and Christian de Duve?

rubric.why: Golgi's work led to the identification of the Golgi apparatus.
rubric.description: Identifies the structure discovered by Camillo Golgi.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the Golgi apparatus.

rubric.why: De Duve is associated with the discovery of lysosomes.
rubric.description: Identifies the structure discovered by Christian de Duve.

modelAnswer: Camillo Golgi discovered the Golgi apparatus.

items.followUp: Name the main stages of the cell cycle.

rubric.why: The cell cycle is defined as an ordered series of events in a cell.
rubric.description: States that the cell cycle is a sequence or series of events in a cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as an ordered series or sequence of cellular events.

rubric.why: The defining sequence culminates in cell division and formation of daughter cells.
rubric.description: States that the sequence leads to cell division, producing two daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the outcome of the cycle as division into two daughter cells.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the ordered series of events that takes place in a cell.
It leads to the cell's division into two daughter cells.

items.followUp: Why did Haeckel propose the kingdom Protista?

rubric.why: The earlier classification system could not adequately place all organisms.
rubric.description: Explains that the two-kingdom system was inadequate for classifying some organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the limitation of the Plantae–Animalia classification.

rubric.why: The third kingdom provided a place for organisms that did not fit the two original kingdoms.
rubric.description: Identifies the addition of Protista for organisms such as unicellular organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Protista was added to accommodate organisms that did not fit well in Plantae or Animalia.

modelAnswer: The two-kingdom system could not adequately classify some organisms, especially many unicellular forms.
Haeckel therefore added the kingdom Protista to accommodate organisms that did not fit well in Plantae or Animalia.

items.followUp: Why is the Houbara bustard considered a threatened migratory bird?

rubric.why: A key fact about the Houbara bustard is its seasonal migration to Pakistan.
rubric.description: States that the Houbara bustard migrates to Pakistan in winter.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its winter migration to Pakistan, for example from Central Asia.

rubric.why: Hunting has contributed to its threatened status and the need for protection.
rubric.description: Notes that it is threatened by hunting or needs protection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning hunting as a threat or identifying the need to protect the bird.

modelAnswer: The Houbara bustard is a migratory bird that visits Pakistan in winter, travelling from Central Asia.
It is threatened by hunting and therefore needs protection.
